prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Interactive Pet Customization Stage [adoption, redesign]: predicted +12.0%, measured +3.7% (p=0.294632), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Defer Sign-In After Pet Selection [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +10.0%, measured +0.3% (p=0.907176), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Pet Generation Waiting Screen Tips & Timer [home, wait_info]: predicted +8.0%, measured +8.9% (p=0.000775), won

Previous lessons:
(none yet)

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Adding tips and a timer to waiting screens (wait_info) was helpful (+8.9% measured, p=0.000775), slightly exceeding the predicted +8.0%.
Redesigning the pet customization stage (redesign) showed no clear effect (+3.7%, p=0.295), falling far short of the +12.0% prediction.
Deferring sign-in after pet selection (reorder/sign_in) showed no clear effect (+0.3%, p=0.907), far below the +10.0% prediction.
Predictions for redesigns and step reordering were significantly too optimistic.
